component.name: Loom
component.summary: Live build-order assistant for Age of Empires II: DE

description.p: Loom watches Age of Empires II: Definitive Edition's HUD by screen capture, reads the total villager count and the game clock off it several times a second, and uses those two numbers to drive a build order — showing the step to do now, the step after it, whether you are on pace, and how your villagers are spread across food, wood, gold and stone versus what the build wants.

It never touches the game process. Nothing is injected, no memory is read and no file the game is still writing is opened; Loom takes pixels in and puts an overlay out. Recorded games are read only after a match has ended, because the file contains both players' orders including everything the fog of war hid.

ul.li: A transparent, click-through overlay that stays above the game
Build orders in the RTS Overlay JSON format, so community builds load unchanged
A step checklist that distinguishes what Loom observed from what it assumed
Idle Town Centre and housed alerts read off the production queue
Per-game statistics with graphs, and APM tracking
The stock HUD and the Anne_HK Better UI mod are both read

description.p: Loom is early software. It reads the screen, so it meets a different machine in every resolution, display scaling and HUD mod out there. Reports with your resolution and desktop are the fastest way problems get fixed.
